claim_under_test: Each named bypass of the ClaimGate enforcement layer now fails CLOSED, demonstrated by running the attack rather than by reading the code.
claim_ceiling: E2, supervised execution. Every result below is DETECTION, never PREVENTION. `git commit --no-verify` still skips the local hook, and CI config lives in the same repo it gates, so anyone who can edit .github/workflows can still disable the checks wholesale. That ceiling is owner-only to raise (branch protection, required checks, CODEOWNERS) and is NOT closed here.
method: Each attack was executed against the working tree, before and after the repair, and the observed exit code recorded. No attack was assessed by inspection alone.

attacks.name: hostile-fixture laundering
attacks.defeats: the entire CI receipt sweep, at zero cost and with no edit to any checker
attacks.mechanism: ci_receipt_sweep.is_excluded() skipped any path under a fixture PREFIX. A path prefix cannot distinguish poison written on purpose from poison parked there.
attacks.repair: 88 fixtures pinned by sha256 in claimgate_plugin/fixtures/sweep_fixture_manifest.json with the exit each checker must return. Unpinned files under a fixture root are swept as ordinary receipts. A pinned fixture that changes digest, disappears, or stops producing its recorded exit fails the job and is NOT covered by --max-failures.

attacks.name: stdlib shadowing
attacks.defeats: every digest, parse and check the gate performs
attacks.mechanism: checkers were run as [sys.executable, <script path>], which puts claimgate_plugin/ on sys.path[0]; a file claimgate_plugin/json.py is then imported instead of the stdlib json.

after.note: rejected; the shadow file is now a submodule, not top-level json

attacks.repair: ci_receipt_sweep._checker_argv runs each checker via an isolated trampoline: python3 -I -c 'sys.path.append(<repo root>); runpy.run_module("claimgate_plugin.<name>")'. -I drops PYTHONPATH and user site-packages so no environment variable steers resolution.
attacks.residual_found_during_repair: The first repair used sys.path.insert(0, REPO), which put the REPO ROOT ahead of the stdlib — a json.py one directory up defeated it again (measured: exit 0). Corrected to append, so the stdlib wins every top-level name (measured: exit 1). Found by an independent reviewer, not by the author.

attacks.name: ledger forgery
attacks.defeats: the durable gate-run record, i.e. the only evidence that a gate ever ran
attacks.mechanism: gate_ledger chained records with unkeyed SHA-256 and verify() accepted any caller-supplied path. A whole self-consistent chain plus matching head anchor can be regenerated by anyone who can write the file; an unkeyed chain proves CONSISTENCY, never AUTHORSHIP.
attacks.reproduction: regenerate N chained lines from GENESIS with a matching gate_ledger.head.json, then: python3 claimgate_plugin/gate_ledger.py verify <forged.jsonl>
attacks.repair: (1) PATH ALLOWLIST — exactly one authoritative ledger; any other path is labelled NON-AUTHORITATIVE and can never certify a run. (2) HMAC-SHA256 per record, keyed from outside writable repo content; a key path inside the repo is REFUSED, not trusted. Absent key => records are written UNKEYED and verify reports CONSISTENT_UNATTRIBUTED, which is never upgraded to 'verified'.
attacks.honest_ceiling: HMAC raises forgery from 'edit a file' to 'hold the key'. Anyone who can READ the key can still forge. The 35 pre-existing local records are UNKEYED and are reported as unattributed rather than being backfilled — a backfilled line would be a fabricated gate run.

attacks.name: orphan-ceiling swap
attacks.defeats: the orphan ratchet, letting a new ungated receipt land invisibly
attacks.mechanism: the baseline compared a COUNT (orphan_receipts_max). A count is fungible: delete one historical orphan, add one brand-new ungated receipt, total unchanged.
attacks.reproduction: mv <a frozen orphan> /tmp/ && printf '{"classification":"canonical","claim_under_test":"snuck in","all_pass":true}' > system_v8/sneaked_receipt.json && python3 claimgate_plugin/ci_orphan_ratchet.py

after.observed: orphans now=2875 frozen=2875 new=1 mutated=0 resolved=1

attacks.repair: claimgate_plugin/ci_orphan_baseline.json freezes the exact SET: 2875 paths, each with its sha256. NEW ORPHAN and MUTATED both fail; RESOLVED is reported for deliberate pruning.
attacks.also_closed: MUTATION — editing a grandfathered orphan in place was previously invisible. Measured: MUTATED claimgate_plugin/results/lean_stack_v0.json (bacdcd16fdf8 -> 0666f1758e22), exit 1.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: top-level array skips every check
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: both checkers did `if not isinstance(receipt, dict): return 0`, so wrapping a receipt in [...] bypassed the poison scan and every recompute.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: scan whatever shape arrived; the recursive walk already descends lists. Only the floor check still requires an object, and says so.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: RF_STORE env deletes the locked-floor check
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: an unreadable or missing store returned None, which is indistinguishable from 'no floors are locked'. An attacker-influenceable env var silently removed a whole check.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: a CONFIGURED but unusable store is infrastructure breakage and PARKs (exit 3). Unset RF_STORE still means 'nothing locked'.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: unsupported aggregate op reports a pass while checking nothing
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.reproduction: receipt declaring recompute op 'median' -> 'recompute_veto: pass — 0 claimed value(s) re-derived'
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: `if op not in AGG: continue` skipped the job, and the summary line then reported a pass over zero checks.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: an op this gate cannot recompute is a VETO. Adding the op is the fix; skipping it is not.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: live scope omitted two live surfaces
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: LIVE_ROOTS held system_v8, claimgate_plugin, ratchet_contract while CLAUDE.md names system_v8/, MODEL_DOSSIER/, ROOT/ as the live surfaces. A receipt written to the current-era docs home was never swept at live scope.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: MODEL_DOSSIER and ROOT added to LIVE_ROOTS.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: deleting the ledger verifies clean
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: read_lines() turns any read error into [], zero records skip every per-record check, and the head anchor is optional — so `chain: OK`, exit 0. The tamper-evidence design covered edits and interior deletions but not deletion of the whole file.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: an absent authoritative ledger is LEDGER ABSENT and fails; an empty body beside an existing head anchor is reported as truncation to zero.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: killing numba silently deletes the summation-order veto
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.reproduction: d=$(mktemp -d); printf 'def njit(*a,**k): raise RuntimeError("disabled")\n' > $d/numba.py; printf '{"classification":"claim","raw_x":[1e16,1.0,-1e16],"sum_x":1.0}' > f.json; PYTHONPATH=$d python3 claimgate_plugin/recompute_veto.py f.json
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: ordered_sum_check swallowed every exception into ran=False, and the caller read ran=False as 'no veto'. The check built specifically for the compensated-vs-ordered problem evaporated whenever numba was unavailable — including by an injected PYTHONPATH.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: the failure reason is returned instead of a bare False, and a check that could not run is a VETO. An unverifiable claim is not a verified one.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: unicode-escaped key evades claim_bearing
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.reproduction: write {"claim\u005funder\u005ftest":"x","bad":999} — valid JSON decoding to the real key — then check claim_bearing()
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: claim_bearing scanned RAW BYTES for literal markers, so any JSON string escape hid the key while json.loads still decoded it.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: byte markers are a fast path only; anything that parses is also judged on its PARSED keys at any depth, and anything that does not parse is treated as claim-bearing so a checker states the reason.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: the SAME laundering bypass survived in the orphan detector
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: orphan_receipt_detector._is_excluded was `"hostile" in parts and "fixtures" in parts` — the identical path-shape exclusion repaired in the sweep. Fixing one and not the other left the hole fully open one file over: a claim dropped into any directory whose path contained both words never entered the orphan baseline.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.repair: the detector now reads the same digest-pinned manifest; only a pinned fixture is excluded.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.lesson: a bypass repaired in one place is not repaired. The same shape has to be swept for everywhere it was copied.

fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.name: sweep failure budgets are still count-substitutable
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.cause: ci_ratchet_baseline.json still records legacy_intake_failures_max and legacy_recompute_vetoes_max as COUNTS. This is the same fungibility repaired for the orphan set: fix one old failing receipt and a free slot opens for one new poisoned one while CI stays within budget.
fail_open_defects_found_by_independent_r.why_not_repaired_here: It needs the same path+digest freeze the orphan set now has, over two more corpora. Recorded rather than quietly carried, so it is not mistaken for closed.

not_closed: git commit --no-verify still bypasses the local pre-commit hook entirely (measured).

CI configuration lives in the repo it gates, so editing .github/workflows disables these checks. Owner-only fix: branch protection, required ClaimGate check, CODEOWNERS on .github/** and claimgate_plugin/**, block force-push and deletion.
Branch protection returned 404 when queried. A 404 can also mean insufficient API permission, so this must be confirmed in GitHub Settings by the owner rather than inferred.
The ledger key is not provisioned. Until CLAIMGATE_LEDGER_KEY_FILE points at a key outside the repo, every record is written UNKEYED and the ledger proves consistency only.
regression_guarantee: All four attacks and all four fail-open defects are preserved as executable reproductions in this file, and the fixture corpus that drives them is digest-pinned. Re-pinning the manifest or re-freezing the orphan set to make a job green erases the finding — that is the same error as raising a ratchet ceiling.
